items.title: What happened to the original Fountain
items.claim: Marcel Duchamp submitted Fountain, a signed urinal, to the Society of Independent Artists in New York in 1917. What is true about the original object today?

options.text: It is in the Met's permanent collection
It was lost; existing versions are 1960s replicas authorised by Duchamp
It is on permanent display at MoMA
It was destroyed at the original exhibition

items.reveal_title: The original was lost; all 'Fountains' are later replicas
items.reveal:
The Society of Independent Artists never displayed it; the original disappeared. From the 1960s Duchamp authorised replicas, now in collections including the Tate and Centre Pompidou.

A 2004 survey of 500 art-world figures voted Fountain the most influential artwork of the 20th century.
items.why: Conceptual art's value can attach to the idea, not the original object.

items.title: The most expensive painting sold
items.claim: Which painting holds the auction record set in November 2017?
items.reveal:
The Leonardo attribution to Salvator Mundi remains contested by some scholars. The buyer was reportedly acting for the Saudi crown prince.

The painting has not been publicly displayed since the sale.
items.why: Attribution debates and market records are intertwined in the history of major paintings.

items.title: Kandinsky and abstraction
items.claim: Wassily Kandinsky's 1911 book Concerning the Spiritual in Art argued for non-representational painting drawing on what analogy?

options.text: Music as a purely formal art moving the soul

items.reveal:
Kandinsky argued colour and form could affect viewers directly, as harmony and rhythm do in music.

His Compositions and Improvisations are titled after musical genres.
items.why: Abstraction needed a theoretical framework before audiences could read it as art.
